# Lindblad Program Cost

This repository studies the number of independent quantum program copies required to simulate an unknown single-jump Lindblad evolution.

Start with README.md for the results and science/model.md for the exact access model. The jump is Frobenius normalized, the program is its vectorization with an unnormalized maximally entangled vector, and error is one half of the diamond norm.

## Scientific routes

- Full argument: science/model.md -> science/conjugation.md -> science/dimension_cost.md -> science/upper_bound.md -> science/interpretation.md.
- Exact minimax assumptions, ancillary resources, and program orientation: science/model.md.
- Haar/Choi inequality for CP branches, including postselection: science/conjugation.md.
- Physical reference flag, fixed-input damping reduction, finite-copy lower bound, and short-time corollary: science/dimension_cost.md.
- Universal WML processor, invariant algebra, remainder estimates, and integer sample budget: science/upper_bound.md.
- Explicit collective processor for known-sink rank-one jumps, including all-time scaling: science/rank_one_processor.md.
- Physical meaning, time regimes, and counted resources: science/interpretation.md.
- Source attribution and model comparisons: references/RELATED_WORK.md and references/references.bib.
- Executable finite checks, tolerances, and recorded outputs: verification/README.md.

## Learning route

The single educational anchor is John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (Cambridge University Press, 2018), using the author-hosted manuscript and chapter files. Read learning/WATROUS_BRIDGE.md for the section map, notation translation, and local derivations.

learning/MILESTONES.md contains exactly 30 project-defined milestones: M01-M14 are background/preliminaries, and M15-M30 are narrative/innovation. The map is learner independent. Each entry gives a central question, understanding target, earlier dependencies and story role, conceptual connection, and source pointers.

Use the bridge and milestones together; use the science pages as the authoritative statements and proofs. The four-dimensional worked example explains the fixed-input branch without replacing the general theorem.

## Essential distinctions

The main lower bound permits all fixed CPTP processors, including collective and adaptive processing with a deterministic copy cap. It is stronger in scope than an algorithm-specific lower bound.

The universal matching law is Theta(d t^2 / epsilon) for d >= 4, 0 < t <= 1, and 0 < epsilon <= t^2 / 256. The finite-copy lower bound holds at all times, but does not imply a universal quadratic long-time law.

The known-sink rank-one family has a separate all-time matching law Theta(d (1 - exp(-t/2))^2 / epsilon), for epsilon <= (1 - exp(-t/2))^2 / 16. Its constructive upper bound must not be transferred to arbitrary jumps.

The conjugation fidelity and WML upper scaling are inherited results. The dissipative reduction and its arbitrary-processor dimension converse are the central contribution. The bibliography preserves exact source versions.

Copy sufficiency does not imply gate efficiency. The program-preparation cost, an inverse preparation oracle, a classical description of the jump, and expected-cost stopping rules are outside the stated resource guarantee.

The written proofs establish the general claims. The numerical checks test specific identities and conventions.
